findings.title: Rule 3's 95% interval reproduces, but its upper end sits at zero and the interval includes the rule's -0.05 margin
findings.evidence: paired_intervals gives prose v15 - quotes = -0.123, [-0.243, -0.003] (bootstrap seed 11, 2,000 resamples), exactly as reported. Over 50 questions v15 wins 6, loses 15 and ties 29 (two-sided sign test p = 0.078). With 2,000 resamples, 24 of 50 other bootstrap seeds (1-50) put the upper end at 0 or above (range -0.010 to +0.003). With 100,000 resamples the upper end is -0.003 to 0.000. 2.2% of bootstrap means are >= 0, and 11.5% are >= -0.05 (the rule's margin).
findings.implication: Under the pre-registration the verdict stands: 0.583 < 0.707 - 0.05, so rule 3 is not met. The interval behind it does not show that v15 is clearly worse than quotes, or that it misses by more than the margin. The interval is right at zero and contains -0.05. The write-up should call it 'not met, within chance', as the pre-registration said a close rule-3 verdict would be read, and should not describe [-0.243, -0.003] as a robust exclusion of zero.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and could not. Every number checks out against the saved per-question rows in /home/user/integratedai/cie/docs/benchmarks/brain/test/test5k/report.json, and the rule-3 verdict does not change.

- **The interval reproduces.** brain_test.paired_intervals, which uses memory_test.paired_ci with seed 11 and 2,000 resamples, gives prose v15 - quotes = -0.123, [-0.243, -0.003]. The family means are 0.583 and 0.707.
- **Win/loss count and sign test.** Over the 50 prose questions v15 wins 6, loses 15 and ties 29. The exact two-sided sign test gives p = 0.078.
- **The upper end depends on the seed.** With seeds 1 to 50 at 2,000 resamples, 24 seeds put the upper end at or above 0. The range is -0.010 to +0.003, and the lower end runs from -0.257 to -0.237. At 100,000 resamples the upper end is -0.003 or -0.000 on seeds 1 to 5.
- **Tail shares.** With seed 11, 2.05% of bootstrap means are at or above 0 and 11.45% are at or above -0.05 at 2,000 resamples. At 100,000 resamples the shares are 2.2% and 11.4%. The finding's 2.2% and 11.5% mix the two runs, which is immaterial.
- **Normal approximation agrees.** The standard error is 0.063, so the mean is 1.96 SE below 0 and only 1.17 SE below the -0.05 margin. The interval clearly contains -0.05.

The pre-registration supports the finding's reading. It says "Rule 3 is decided within chance", that the standard error (about 0.056) is larger than the 0.05 margin, and that "a close verdict is read with them [the paired intervals]". paired_intervals is documented as "Reported, not decided on."

The verdict stands as the finding itself says: 0.583 < 0.657, so rule 3 is not met and the claim (rules 1-4) is not met.

One limit on the finding: no write-up yet calls [-0.243, -0.003] a robust exclusion of zero. Only the raw report.md exists, and it prints the JSON. So the recommendation guards a future write-up rather than correcting text that is already there. Its factual content is still concretely confirmed, and it is a fair low-severity caution about how to describe the result.

findings.title: One free-text question was wrongly rejected as a yes/no question
findings.evidence: prose-812-032, "Can you remind me what Support actually changed on BlueHaven's tenant optimizer profile during the 03/12 maintenance window ...?", was rejected as 'yes/no question'. In brain_writers.py, YES_NO_RE matches the opening 'Can'. WH_ASKED_RE, which rescues 'tell me what', 'remember what' and 'recall what', has no entry for 'remind me'. The other 6 rejections hold up under the pre-registered checks: 2 asked more than one question, 2 had one-token facts (error_code=..., normalize_path_first), 1 question held 4 of the 5 content words of its fact, and 1 descriptive question repeated the title. Re-running status and collect in scratch reproduces the kept and rejected files byte for byte.
findings.implication: No effect on the mix: 54 free-text questions were kept and the mix needs 50. The pool that seed 810 drew from was missing one valid question. This is a false positive in the frozen checks to note in the write-up. It cannot be fixed after the fact.

verdict.reason: The regex part is true, but the main claim is wrong. Nothing valid was lost. In brain_writers.py (unchanged since the freeze at 723a70b), YES_NO_RE matches the opening "Can". WH_ASKED_RE has no "remind me" entry, so question_words returns []. That is why prose-812-032 got the label "yes/no question". But collect runs _why_question first and only reaches _why_prose if the question passes. I re-ran the checks on all 6 rejected free-text questions against the sealed packet text (test5k_prose_812.packets.jsonl). For prose-812-032, _why_prose returns "answer fact shorter than 2 words": its second fact, "kv_prefetch:false", is one token, the same failure as prose-812-035 and prose-812-039. The pre-registration (line 130) lists "a fact shorter than 2 words" as a rejection reason. So the question was correctly rejected under the frozen rules, and the yes/no check only got there first. The finding missed that this question has a one-token fact while counting two others that did. Its claims that a valid question was wrongly rejected and that the pool seed 810 drew from lacked one valid question are false. At most the stored reason is the wrong label. Kept/rejected counts (54/6), the mix and every score are unaffected.

verdict.reason:
I checked the finding's claims one by one and they hold. It overstates two small points, and it does not affect the result.

Confirmed:
(1) Step 1's printed output was not saved anywhere. A search of the scratchpad for logs written after run_brain_1.sh finds only brain/run_brain_2.log. docs/benchmarks/brain/test/ has only run_brain_2.log too. run_brain_1.sh prints its output to the terminal and never writes it to a file.
(2) arms.json stores only these fields: arm, label, file, single/plans/router (the lesson paths), seconds, answers, questions_sha256 and haystack_sha256. brain_test.ask() builds that record at about line 519 and adds no lesson hash and no hash seed. report.json and report.md copy the same fields. Nothing in src/cie/eval/brain_test.py reads PYTHONHASHSEED. The only hash-seed values are the exports in run_brain_2.sh (seed 0, and seed 1 for v15_seed1).
(3) The lesson files' modification times are all before the freeze at 23:49:24: single_lessons.json, plan_lessons.json and router.json at 2026-10-10 22:20:02, fb50/lessons.json on Oct 7 and plan_lessons_v13.json on Oct 9. Their sha256 prefixes today (ee8b9d05…, de756122…, 20e9c050…, afa4e7d9…, 64cf5b30…) match the Frozen table in the pre-registration. The three files in docs/benchmarks/brain/lessons/ show no changes in git.

Where the finding overstates:
- The haystack can be checked from a record. Step 1's 16-character sha256 of the haystack.json file was not saved, but arms.json and banks.json store a full haystack_sha256 for every arm. That value is a fingerprint of the benchmark root plus the sorted document ids, not of the file's bytes. haystack.json itself is kept: the docs copy is byte-identical to the scratchpad file, which was last changed at 23:49:58, and its sha256 starts d2e3d43c40dbc5bc.
- The batch names given to writers_test.js can also be read back. writers/test_out holds one <batch>.jsonl file per batch, and the two status.json files list all 10 batches as complete.

So what truly cannot be read from a record is narrower than stated: the lesson hashes at run time and the hash seed. Both can only be inferred, from modification times and today's hashes, and from the script. The finding is accurate on these, rates itself low severity and says nothing contradicts the protocol. The scores and the decision stay as they are.

findings.title: Free text: v15 loses on how it cuts and ranks passages, not on which documents it picks
findings.evidence: I re-ran Brain.prose and the quotes search from the banks. Both arms' answers came out byte-identical for all 51 questions (the 50 prose questions plus desc-811-002). Documents are not the cause: the gold document is v15's first FTS document on 49/50 questions and its second on 1. Both arms quote the gold document on 50/50. 105 of 106 facts sit in v15's first 20 passages, the pool quote_answer reads (quotes: 106/106). Ranking differs: the first passage holding a fact has mean rank 2.70 in v15 (top 3 for 73/106 facts) against 0.61 in quotes (98/106). Quotes ranks it higher for 55 facts, v15 for 8. Gold passages in the 20-passage pool: 6.5 vs 8.5. I swapped one factor at a time (cf.json; v15 = 0.583, quotes = 0.707 reproduced). On v15's own 5 documents and bank text: BM25 instead of IDF-share 0.670 (+0.087); chunk(1000, 120 overlap) instead of windows(600,1000) 0.663 (+0.080); both 0.717. Text source (bank vs render_doc) makes about 0 difference. The 5-document set scores at or above the all-documents search in every pairing. Most of chunk's gain is the 120-char overlap (cf_overlap.json): with overlap 0, quotes itself falls to 0.597 and v15-with-chunk to 0.610. Of the 22 facts quotes got and v15 missed: 14 were in a passage ranked 0-9 but other sentences, often from other documents' passages mixed in, filled the 1,100-char cap; 3 were ranked 10-19; 4 (812-015, 812-038, 812-025 x2) open the next window right after a sentence v15 quoted, where quote_answer's next-sentence rule cannot reach; 1 was outside the pool. On the 259-document small set the gap is the same: v15 0.617 vs quotes 0.743, -0.127 [-0.223, -0.03].
findings.implication: The fix belongs in FactBank.passages ranking (IDF-share counts only whether each question word appears, with no term frequency or length weighting, so passages tie and other documents' passages mix in) and in its cutting (no overlap). Retrieving more documents would not help. Scale does not explain it either.

verdict.reason:
The finding's numbers reproduce, but the reading it puts on them does not hold up. Its two main claims, "not on which documents it picks" and "the cause is IDF-share having no term-frequency or length weighting", are both contradicted when I apply the finding's own swap-one-factor method.

What checks out:
- I compared cf.json with the official answers. 50/50 of v15's answers and 50/50 of quotes' answers are byte-identical, and they score 0.583 and 0.707.
- The gold document is v15's first FTS document on 49/50 questions and its second on 1. Both arms cite the gold document on 50/50.
- 105 of 106 facts are in v15's 20-passage pool and 106/106 in quotes'. Facts in the top 3: 73 vs 98. Gold passages in the pool: 6.54 vs 8.48.
- The lost facts split 14 / 3 / 4 / 1.
- All the cf and cf_overlap scores reproduce. On the 259-document small set, v15 scores 0.617 and quotes 0.743, a gap of -0.127 [-0.223, -0.03].

What is refuted:

1. **Documents do matter.** The finding only tried more documents. I kept v15's own IDF-share ranking and windows(600,1000) cutting unchanged and changed only k_docs in FactBank.passages (scripts c4.py and c7.py in postrun/diag_refute).
   - test5k: k=1 scores 0.717 (above quotes' 0.707), k=2 0.677, k=3 0.607, k=5 0.583 (exactly v15), k=8 0.553.
   - Small set: k=1 scores 0.720, against 0.617 at k=5.
   - Cutting to one document is worth +0.134. That is the largest single factor, bigger than the ranking swap (+0.087) or the cutting swap (+0.080), and on test5k it closes the whole gap by itself.
   - So v15 loses because passages from the 2nd to 5th documents push out the first document's passages. Which documents it picks is a primary cause.

2. **The claimed mechanism is wrong.** I re-ran the BM25 swap on v15's 5 documents with different title weights (c6.py).
   - Body-only BM25 (title weight 0), which adds exactly the term-frequency and length weighting the finding says is missing, scores 0.550. That is worse than IDF-share's 0.583.
   - With the title column weighted 1.0 it scores 0.630; at 2.5 it scores 0.670, which reproduces the reviewer's number.
   - So the whole +0.087 comes from title matching. Every passage of a document carries the same title, so this mostly acts as a whole-document boost.
   - The code also contradicts "passages tie and other documents' passages mix in". In engine.py, passages() sorts by (-score, doc rank, i), so a tie goes to the higher-ranked document, which is the gold document on 49/50 questions. Another document's passage can only get ahead with a strictly higher score.

3. **The fix it proposes is incomplete.** The finding says the fix belongs in term-frequency/length ranking and in cutting, and that retrieving more documents would not help. The second part is true. But keeping only the top document, or ranking passages by their document, closes the gap with no change to ranking or cutting.

The overlap observation (the next-sentence rule cannot reach a sentence that opens the next window) is real. It is a secondary factor.

**Effect on the test result:** none. This is a diagnosis after the fact; rule 3 is still not met.

findings.title: Check after the run (not a result): with quotes' passage search, v15 would have met rule 3
findings.evidence: Swapping v15's prose route for cie.eval.brain_test.Passages (BM25, 60 passages, quote_answer) gives answers identical to quotes on all 50 prose questions, so prose = 0.707, difference 0.000, rule 3 met. The only other question routed to prose (desc-811-002) scores 0 either way, so single, multi and not_found are unchanged and the mean over families would be 0.875. Smaller changes that also meet the 0.657 threshold: keep v15's 5 documents, bank text and windows and switch only to BM25: 0.670 (-0.037 vs quotes, 95% CI [-0.143, 0.067]). Switch only to chunk cutting: 0.663 (-0.043, [-0.133, 0.047]). v15's 5 documents with quotes' passages and BM25: 0.723 (+0.017, [-0.043, 0.083]). Caveats: I tried 17 variants after seeing the test answers, so the best one is optimistic. On the development set v15 had led (0.663 vs 0.654), and the pre-registration put the standard error at about 0.056, more than the 0.05 margin.
findings.implication: Rule 3 failed on a component the pre-registration says is shared ('the same quoting code'). The quoting code is the same, but passage retrieval and cutting differ. A fix (quotes' search, or BM25 plus overlapping chunks inside the brain) needs a fresh test set; these test numbers cannot support it.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this finding and could not. Every concrete claim holds when checked independently. My scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-integratedai/275b943f-979b-5741-9af5-2a07879accea/scratchpad/postrun/diagnosis_refute/: v1.py, v2.py, and v3.py, which rebuilt the variants through the real Brain.prose path rather than reusing the reviewer's harness.

(1) Routing. v15 sent all 50 prose questions to the prose route. The only other question routed to prose is desc-811-002, which scores 0 for both v15 and quotes.

(2) Same quoting code. Both arms call quote_answer (cie/src/cie/retrieval/answer.py:188). It reads only each item's 'detail' and 'summary', from the first 20 items. So feeding v15's prose route from brain_test.Passages.search(q, 60) gives quotes' answers by construction. My rerun matched quotes' answer strings on 50 of 50 questions: prose 0.707, difference 0.000, so rule 3 is met. Quotes declined no question, so the swap adds no false "not found" answers (still 0 of 195) and rule 4 is unaffected.

(3) Family scores. Single, multi and not_found stay at 0.8214, 0.9722 and 1.0, and prose becomes 0.7067, so the mean over families is 0.8751 (the finding's 0.875).

(4) The smaller variants reproduce exactly:
- chunk cutting only (monkeypatching engine.windows to bench_enterprise.chunk): 0.663, difference -0.043;
- BM25 only, keeping v15's 5 documents, bank text and windows: 0.670, difference -0.037;
- v15's 5 documents with quotes' Passages and BM25: 0.723, difference +0.017.
The baseline rerun reproduces v15's answers on 50 of 50. The 95% intervals differ from the finding's only in the third decimal, for example [-0.147, 0.067] against [-0.143, 0.067]. That is because the reviewer bootstrapped over question ids in sorted order; paired_ci uses seed 11 and depends on order.

(5) The caveats are accurate. Of the 17 variants in cf.json and cf_overlap.json, chunks without overlap and BM25 over all documents on bank text fail. On development v15 led 0.663 to 0.654, and the standard error of about 0.056 is stated in the pre-registration.

(6) The diagnosis is concrete. With v15's own 5 documents, quotes' passage cutting and ranking does better than quotes. So the loss comes from how passages are cut and ranked within the documents, not from which documents are chosen or from the quoting code. The pre-registration describes the shared part only as 'the same quoting code', which is true, so the finding does not contradict it.

The finding is labelled a check after the run, not a result, and it says that a fix needs a fresh test set. The pre-registered decision therefore stands: rule 3 is not met and the claim (rules 1 to 4) is not met.

findings.title: Single questions where v15 is below the best other arm: 7 (none in multi). 3 are the brain's own router or planner errors
findings.evidence: No multi question has v15 below another arm; ticket_link-status-129 is 0 for both v15 and v13. The 7 single questions, with the brain-specific causes first. desc-811-002 (v1/v2 1.0): the router sent it to prose (prose 0.92). The question asks 'when the SLA is due ... and how to handle the loaner laptops'; signals how_do=1, long=0.9 and when=0 (the 'when' signal did not fire on 'Do you know when'), and the quoted passages hold no date. desc-811-033 (v1/v2 'evaluation'): the bank holds 'Okta SSO' as a person entity (person:okta sso), so the planner counted it as a named start and answered 'BlueHarbor Labs' via participants_external_of -> related_account. reads_asked_field returns True for any plan that follows a link, so the field check (wanted: stage 3.0) never ran. meeting_customer-062 (quotes 1.0): the planner read meeting_id ('ff-20270309-ceru-8372'). The field check passed because the word 'meeting' gives meeting_id weight 0.5, equal to customer_company's 0.5. The planner's second plan had 'customer_company -> Cerulean Tech'. 002 and 033 are the only single questions where v15 is below v1; v15 is above v1 on 5, all through the planner.
findings.implication: Three fixable faults: the 'when' signal only fires at the start of a question; product names are stored as people; and the field check is skipped for linked plans and passes on field-name ties. Each costs about 0.01 on single. Rule 1 was still met (+0.028).

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute it and could not. The counts and the three per-question diagnoses are correct. The finding's "three fixable faults" implication is overstated, though, and part of its stated mechanism is wrong.

**Confirmed (report.json rows, answer files, and the brain rebuilt read-only on factbank_v2.sqlite with the run's lessons and router)**
- The counts hold. Exactly 7 single questions have v15 below the best other arm: meeting_attendees-059, meeting_customer-062, meeting_date-043, desc-811-002, desc-811-019, desc-811-028 and desc-811-033. No multi question does, and ticket_link-status-129 scores 0 in every arm.
- desc-811-002 and desc-811-033 are the only single questions where v15 is below v1. v15 is above v1 on 5 (jira_sla-027, jira_status-006, linear_issue_assignee-239, pr_repo-015, linear_due-164), all on route plan. That is (5-2)/109 = +0.028, matching rule 1.
- **desc-811-002:** route prose with prose 0.9225. The signals are how_do=1, long=0.9, when=0, and interrogative_kind is None. The quoted answer holds no date. The planner's best plan (sla_due_at → 2026-03-13) and the engine would both have given the right answer.
- **desc-811-033:** the bank holds person:okta sso, and Planner.about gives start_named=True. The plan is Okta SSO → participants_external_of → related_account, answering BlueHarbor Labs. reads_asked_field returns True at its first line because best.path is non-empty. wanted gives stage 3.0.
- **meeting_customer-062:** the best plan reads meeting_id (score 0.697), ahead of customer_company (0.571). wanted gives meeting_id 0.5 and customer_company 0.5.
- The other 4 questions take route fact, and v15's answer equals v1's (the engine's errors, inherited), so "3 are the brain's own" holds.

**Corrections to the implication**
1. **The 'when' fault is misstated and does not explain 002.** Planner.interrogative_kind counts a question word at the start of any clause (after punctuation, or after and/but/so/then/also), not only at the start of the question. Setting when=1 still routes 002 to prose (0.839), and adding how_do=0 too still gives 0.775. Most of the push to prose comes from the word features w:how (+1.32), w:and (+1.07) and w:do (+0.75). The question really asks two things (a date, then how to handle laptops). And because "and how" opens a second clause, even a question beginning "When is the SLA due..." gives kind None.
2. **The field check does not pass "on ties".** It passes whenever the plan's field has any positive weight (`if want.get(best.field) > 0: return True`). - In 12 of the 15 quotes wins, the gold document is first in both arms.
- Both routes call the same quote_answer. v15 feeds it bank.passages (600-1,000-char windows, top 5 documents). quotes feeds it BM25 chunks (top 60). All 50 prose questions take the prose route in both arms.

What does not hold is the conclusion that the 2,000-char reach "does not explain the failure" and that the cause is sentence choice rather than reach. My scripts are in scratchpad/postrun/meaning/refute_r2/ (r2.py, r3.py, r4.py).

1. On test, quotes reaches more facts within 2,000 chars on 19 questions. quotes wins 10 of them, 9 are ties, and v15 wins none. 10 of the 15 quotes wins are reach-advantage questions; the other 5 have equal reach.
2. All 6 v15 wins are on questions where reach is equal.
3. Within v15 alone, questions where every fact is within 2,000 chars score 0.799. The rest score 0.385.
4. I looked up where the fact-holding passage ranks in each arm for the 15 losses. In quotes it is rank 0 or 1 in 13 of them. In v15 at least one fact sits deeper in 11:
   - rank 2: 036, 037;
   - ranks 3 to 11: 013, 038, 008, 045, 025, 002;
   - rank 17: 010, 015;
   - rank 20: 046.
   quote_answer reads only the first 20 items (pool=20) and penalises lower ranks. So the 24,000-char reach of 1.000 says nothing about what it actually quotes from; the rank-20 passage is never read.
5. Only 4 of the 15 losses (018, 017, 043, 058) are pure sentence-choice failures, with the facts already in v15's top two passages.
6. The finding's own example, prose-812-008, is a reach case. v15 put the author's reply in passage rank 6 (char 6,209) and quotes put it at rank 0.

The 2,000-char reach is how v15's passage windowing and ranking show up in the evidence. So "windowing, not reach" is a false choice, and the write-up's stated evidence is a fair summary of most losses.

The dev comparison does not rescue the claim. The same pattern holds on dev: quotes wins 5 of 8 on questions where it reaches more, while v15 wins only 1 of 7 such questions. Dev reached parity because v15 won other questions. The pre-registration itself says rule 3 is decided within chance.

Two parts are fair: reach alone is not sufficient, and the quotes passage index could replace v15's prose passages as a fix to test on fresh questions. The required correction to the write-up is not supported. The rule 3 verdict is unaffected.

1. Both arms return a bundle of quotes, not a written answer. v15's prose route and the quotes arm both call `quote_answer` (cie/src/cie/retrieval/answer.py; brain.py:389-395; brain_test.ask_quotes). Median answer length on the 50 prose questions is 1,058 chars for v15 and 1,061 for quotes.
2. The scorer pools words across the whole answer. `fact_share` (brain_questions.py:761) runs `evidence_audit.present` once over all the answer's stems: every number in a fact must appear, plus 70% of its stemmed content words. It is not checked one passage at a time, unlike `prose_reach` and the evidence_audit design.
3. prose-812-058 is as described. quotes scored 1.0 because the fact "15% off list for the first 12 months" was matched in its 4th quote. That quote comes from dsid_bb6ef666 ("Segregated fleet scenarios", a 15% discount offered to ApexCare), not from the gold Clearline document.
4. I found two more false credits. On 037, v15 got 0.5 for "spinner fade-in at 80ms" from a different ticket ("Refine button press trajectory..."). On 038, both arms were credited with "Hard constraints from client" from scattered words ("hard-constraint rejection" + "client"), and neither quoted the priority list.
5. There is no judge. On 008 and 017, v15 quoted the gold document but not the answering sentence. It already scores 0 on both, so these are not inflated.

Where the finding is imprecise:
- Taken literally (gold-document quotes only, still pooled), I get v15 0.583→0.573 and quotes 0.707→0.697, with one drop each (037 and 058).
- The finding's numbers need one more restriction: each fact must sit within a single quoted sentence from the gold document. With that, v15 goes to 0.553 with 3 drops (037, 038, 050), matching the finding exactly. quotes goes to 0.667 with 4 drops (017, 038, 050, 058), against the finding's 0.657 and 5.
- The pre-registration already discloses the limit in general terms (Known limits: "No judge... a long quote can hold a fact by chance"; "Free-text answers are quotes, not written answers"). The new part is the concrete wrong-document and pooled credits.

It does not change the verdict. Rule 3 needs v15 ≥ quotes − 0.05. Under every rescoring v15 stays about 0.10–0.12 below quotes (0.553 vs 0.667; 0.573 vs 0.697), so rule 3 is still not met and the claim still fails on free text. The stricter scoring takes a little more from quotes than from v15, so it narrows the gap slightly rather than flipping it. The finding is right that "prose 0.583" means the mean share of answer facts found word-for-word in about 1,060 characters of quotes, not 58% of questions answered.

Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-integratedai/275b943f-979b-5741-9af5-2a07879accea/scratchpad/postrun/meaning/refute_r3/ (seg4.py, gold.json, other.json).

findings.title: The dev set predicted the fact families but not free text. Part of v15's dev free-text score came from a choice made on dev
findings.evidence: Frozen v15 on dev vs test: single 0.804 vs 0.821, multi 1.000 vs 0.972, both held. Prose 0.663 vs 0.583, and quotes 0.654 vs 0.707. Dev paired prose was +0.010 (7 wins, 8 losses); test was -0.123 (6 wins, 15 losses). The pre-registration says the trained router was chosen after reading dev answers, and it lifted dev prose from 0.538 to 0.663 (v15 trained with the rule router vs with the trained router). The difference between the dev and test paired gaps (0.133) is about 1.6 combined SEs, so noise plus dev optimism explains it without a structural break. Test routing itself was near perfect (0.998).
findings.implication: The write-up should say that components tuned on dev carried over on the fact families, but that a dev margin of about 0.01 at 52 questions said nothing reliable about free text. For the next free-text rule, use roughly 150 or more prose questions (SE about 0.036 at the observed spread), or require a replication, and keep router or retrieval choices for prose off the questions used to judge them.

verdict.reason:
I recomputed every number in the finding from the saved answers and they are correct: dev5k/v15b.jsonl against quotes, and test5k/factbank_v15.jsonl against quotes, scored with brain_questions.score. Dev prose was 0.663 vs 0.654, a paired +0.010 (SE 0.055, 7 wins, 8 losses). Test prose was 0.583 vs 0.707, a paired -0.123 (SE 0.063, 6 wins, 15 losses). Combined SE is 0.084, so the 0.133 swing is 1.6 SE. The dev table has rule router 0.538 and trained router 0.663.

What the finding adds beyond those numbers does not hold up:

(1) The router choice made on dev was not optimism. It carried over to test.
- The router was trained only on the training writers' questions.
- I ran the rule router (Router.rule over Brain.signals and the planner) on the 50 test prose questions. It would have sent 8 of 50 to fact routes; on dev it sent 8 of 52.
- The frozen trained router sent all 50 to prose. Those 8 questions earned v15 4.0 points, so the choice added about +0.08 to v15 prose on test (dev: +0.135).

(2) The router-recovered questions explain almost none of the paired swing that decides rule 3.
- On the 8 questions the rule router misroutes, v15 minus quotes is -1/52 on dev and -1.5/50 on test. That is 0.011 of the 0.133 swing.
- On the questions both routers send to prose, v15 vs quotes is 0.625 vs 0.591 on dev (44 questions) and 0.599 vs 0.710 on test (42 questions). That is about 0.12 of the swing, on questions where the dev-made choice plays no part.
- Those 8 questions also fell for quotes (8/8 on dev, 5.5/8 on test). The drop is in the questions, not in the router.

(3) The prose retrieval was not tuned on dev questions.
- FactBank.passages and the brain's prose()/quote_answer path did not change after commit ab56b4a (17:37). Nothing touching prose changed in brain.py between 92e5a03 and the freeze.
- The dev writers' output folder (writers/out) dates from 20:42. So there was no dev-made retrieval choice to cause optimism either.

What is left is noise in the comparison between v15's prose route and plain keyword search. The pre-registration already says this: "Rule 3 is decided within chance", with SE about 0.056, larger than the 0.05 margin. So the main lesson the finding draws (a 0.01 dev margin at 52 questions said nothing reliable) is a restatement of a disclosed limitation, not a new defect. Its suggestion of about 150 prose questions is reasonable, but the stated mechanism ("part of the dev free-text score came from a choice made on dev" helping to explain the miss) is refuted by the test routing and the split above.

No rule outcome or decision changes: rule 3 is still not met and the claim is still not met.

findings.title: Rule 5's +0.55 margin is built into the design: v15 roughly equals the earlier specialists stitched together with a perfect router
findings.evidence: Take the best earlier arm per family with perfect routing: v1 single 0.794, v13 multi 0.889, quotes prose 0.707, and a not-found detector at 1.000. Their mean is 0.848; v15 scores 0.844. v15's gains on single (+0.028) and multi (+0.083) are cancelled by its prose loss (-0.123). No other arm tries every family, so the nearest is 0.291.
findings.implication: Present rule 5 as expected by construction, as the pre-registration itself says. The real news is that one router plus the planner fixes matches the specialists on the fact families with 0.998 route accuracy.

findings.title: Rules 1 and 2 hold and are robust. On single questions v15 is mostly v1 plus a few planner wins
findings.evidence: Single: v15 and v1 differ on only 7 of 109 questions. v15 wins 5, all via the planner (jira_sla, jira_status, linear_issue_assignee, pr_repo, linear_due). It loses 2, both descriptive: desc-811-002 was routed to prose, and desc-811-033 got the planner answer 'BlueHarbor Labs' instead of the stage 'evaluation'. Multi: 3 wins and 0 losses vs v13. Descriptive 0.744 vs v1 0.795 is those 2 questions out of 39. Names 0.553 is identical to v1 on all 10. Project members score 0 of 3 because the answer is a project or document name. Attendees score about 0.6-0.67 because only part of the list comes back. Reviewers score 3 of 3.
findings.implication: Fine to state: no regression on single or multi, and a small multi gain. The descriptive dip is 2 questions and names are a v1 weakness v15 inherits, so neither is a v15 regression. Both are worth fixing, since descriptive questions are the most natural wording.

findings.title: Time and size: 4.6 s per question at 5,000 documents, about 1% of this company's corpus. Rule 6 only covers 259 to 5,000 documents
findings.evidence: v15 median 4,557 ms (p90 5,603) at 5,000 documents, against 587 ms at the 259-document small set: 7.8x the time for 19x the documents. quotes takes 24 ms. Dev median was about 3.4 s, within the preregistered 3-5 s. Big minus small for v15: single -0.029, prose -0.034, multi 0, not_found +0.15, so rule 6 is met. The fresh and seen pools total about 512k documents.
findings.implication: Write 'holds from 259 to 5,000 documents'. Neither accuracy nor latency was measured at the full company size, and latency grows faster than the square root of the corpus.
